"""A lexical 'of' response, attenuated in familiar relational constructions.

The space-prefixed token ' of' is strongly positive by default, even when it
starts a longer word. Quantity, kind, collection, and other common 'of' heads
reduce or reverse this response. Classes of preceding tokens are matched by
spelling, not by parsing sentences. Abstract-noun endings, an 's' ending, and
lack of leading whitespace make small adjustments for unlisted heads.
Other spellings of 'of' and Vietnamese 'của' receive positive baselines;
document-end, reasoning-start, and tool-end markers receive negative ones.
Only the previous token is remembered, and it is cleared between documents.
"""
READS = ()

# Heads of common 'of' constructions, grouped by their ordinary meanings.
KINDS = set('type types kind kinds sort sorts'.split())
LARGE_QUANTITIES = set('number amount amounts lot lots much most majority '
                       'proportion proportions'.split())
SELECTION = set('one some any many few several couple pair plenty none'.split())
COLLECTIONS = set('set sets list lists collection collections series variety '
                  'combination combinations group groups bunch batch mix '
                  'mixture multitude'.split())
EXAMPLES = set('instance instances example examples version versions '
               'copy copies'.split())
PARTS = set('part parts portion portions piece pieces member members fraction '
            'rest remainder subset half'.split())
TOTALITY = set('all each both full percent percentage quantity quantities'.split())
CLASSIFICATION = set('form forms class classes species concept method sense '
                     'case cases'.split())
GEOGRAPHY = set('country state city town region regions area areas field '
                'population kingdom county parish village'.split())
INSTITUTIONS = set('university institute department school'.split())
LINKS = set('out instead because regardless think consist consists consisting composed '
            'made capable aware'.split())
MAGNITUDES = set('range level levels degree size length volume rate rates '
                 'ratio mass concentration weight measure magnitude value '
                 'values probability'.split())
PROCESSES = set('use process purpose development formation production '
                'generation application construction implementation'.split())
TEMPORAL = set('time period age years days year day hours hour months month '
               'weeks week course beginning end'.split())

KNOWLEDGE = set('study analysis understanding knowledge definition description '
                'assessment explanation interpretation representation'.split())
COMMON_RELATIONS = set('result source lack loss importance way quality order '.split())
ARITHMETIC = set('sum product addition subtraction difference quotient total'.split())

GROUPS = (
    (KINDS, -0.44), (LARGE_QUANTITIES, -0.28), (SELECTION, -0.21),
    (COLLECTIONS, -0.06), (EXAMPLES, -0.05), (PARTS, 0.25),
    (TOTALITY, 0.03), (CLASSIFICATION, 0.06), (GEOGRAPHY, 0.20),
    (INSTITUTIONS, -0.17), (LINKS, 0.15), (MAGNITUDES, 0.44),
    (PROCESSES, 0.39), (TEMPORAL, 0.35),
    (KNOWLEDGE, 0.64), (COMMON_RELATIONS, 0.30), (ARITHMETIC, 0.25),
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != document else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if token == ' of':
        word = previous.strip().lower()
        value = 1.00
        if word.endswith('%'):
            value = 0.08
        elif word.endswith(('tion', 'sion', 'ment')):
            value = 0.86
        elif word.isalpha() and previous and not previous[0].isspace():
            value = 1.17
        elif word.isalpha() and word.endswith('s'):
            value = 1.07
        for words, response in GROUPS:
            if word in words:
                value = response
                break
    elif token.strip().lstrip('._-').lower() == 'of':
        value = 0.54
    elif token == '<|endoftext|>':
        value = -0.19
    elif token == '<think>':
        value = -0.23
    elif token == '</tool_call>':
        value = -0.12
    elif token == ' của':
        value = 0.62
    return (document, token), float(value)

It is a "noun of noun" detector: it is strongly active on "of" that follows a head
noun in a relation ("the fingerprint of", "a drawback of", "the ghosts of", "the rules
of"), and nearly silent on "of" that is part of a quantity or fixed phrase ("most of",
"one of", "some of", "amount of", "series of", "list of", "out of", "instead of",
"because of"). Everywhere else it is off.

Plain-terms rule: on "of", predict about 0.6 after a noun; predict about 0.1 after a
quantity or fixed-phrase word; predict 0 on every other token.
"""

QUANTITY = {
    "most", "amount", "one", "series", "list", "collection", "lot", "number", "kind",
    "sort", "type", "bunch", "couple", "few", "many", "some", "all", "both", "none",
    "each", "majority", "portion", "variety", "out", "instead", "because", "ahead",
    "front", "inside", "outside", "regardless", "rather",
}

    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word != "of" or prefix.position == 0:

    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    return None, (0.1 if before in QUANTITY else 0.6)

What it does: the component is mostly silent. Its activation is near zero on almost every
token, and it goes clearly negative on a handful of words about scores, answers and
signatures (English "scores", "signature", "answers", "essay", "key", "results"), on Chinese

the "<tool_call>" tag in chat transcripts. The program outputs a fixed value per word
(its measured mean activation on training text) and 0 for everything else.

Why this simple form: the activation has no compact character-level or positional pattern
(character classes, position in the document, and the previous token all have mean near 0).
Its variance is spread over thousands of tokens. A word list is the only part that reads as
a concept, and it explains only about 1% of the variance. A full token-to-value table
explains about 30% on held-out text, but that is a lookup of about 150k entries and is not
included here.

Carry: none. Reads only the newest token.

# Keys are the token's text, stripped and lower-cased.

    "scores": -0.35,
    "signature": -0.25,
    "signatures": -0.20,
    "answers": -0.15,
    "answer": -0.12,
    "essay": -0.14,
    "score": -0.09,
    "marks": -0.10,
    "results": -0.06,
    "key": -0.06,

    "成绩": -0.16,  # exam score

}

VALUES = {**GRADING, **EXAM_CHINESE, **CHAT_TAG}

    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return None, float(VALUES.get(word, 0.0))

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a signed Polish-spelling signal, with two secondary lexical responses.

Polish letters and function words build a decaying language cue. Within short
alphabetic tokens, y/j, several consonant clusters/stems and some inflections score
positively; i, ie/ia and palatal syllables score negatively. A few grammatical
classes adjust this spelling score. Two separate rules cover the spelling 'spec'
and angle terminology. State stores language evidence and the previous token,
resetting whenever the document changes.
"""
from math import exp

READS = ()
POLISH_LETTERS = set("ąćęłńśźż")
POLISH_CUES = set(
    "jest nie się czy że dla oraz przez przy jak gdy też już są aby będzie "
    "było można tylko owych owego nych ści skiego niej ują ujemy".split()
)
# Each pair of numbers is a baseline and an extra Polish-context response.
# The last flag restricts an ending to tokens without leading whitespace.
GRAMMAR = (
    # Adjectival endings
    (set('ne nej ny nych nym ym'.split()), 0.13, 1.13, True),
    # Feminine case endings
    (set('ej owej'.split()), 0.11, 0.5, True),
    # Nominal endings
    (set('ania anie aniu enia enie ści'.split()), -0.2, -0.25, True),
    # Noun endings in -ja
    (set('acja acje ja'.split()), 0.04, 0.55, True),
    # Palatal syllables
    (set('mi ni si wi zi'.split()), -0.04, -0.67, False),
    # ci syllable
    (set('ci'.split()), -0.12, -1.55, False),
    # Negation
    (set('nie'.split()), 0.49, -0.95, False),
    # Reflexive pronoun
    (set('sie się'.split()), -0.17, -0.54, False),
    # Frequent function words
    (set('aby jak jest'.split()), -0.88, 2.04, False),
    # Prepositions and connectors
    (set('do to w'.split()), 0.0, 0.54, False),
    # Other function words
    (set('a ma o po za'.split()), 0.0, -0.39, False),
    # Demonstrative forms
    (set('tego tej tym'.split()), 0.57, 0.49, False),
)


def spelling(raw, polish):
    s = raw.strip().lower()
    if s.lstrip("._") == "spec":
        return -0.32 - 0.91 * polish - 0.18 * (s != raw.strip())
    if not s.isalpha() or len(s) > 6:
        return 0.0
    no_space = not raw[0].isspace()
    if no_space and s.endswith("ego"):
        return 0.43 + 0.71 * polish
    value = 0.10 * polish
    value += polish * (-0.21 * s.count("i") + 0.29 * s.count("j")
                       + 0.32 * s.count("y"))
    # Spelling patterns. Both their base and language-dependent strengths matter.
    rules = (
        # Conjunction i, isolated letters, and palatal/inflection pieces.
        (s == "i" and not no_space, 0.0, -0.6),
        (no_space and s in {"y", "j"}, 0.0, 0.4),
        (no_space and s in {"ie", "ia", "io"}, 0.0, -0.5),
        (no_space and s == "owe", 0.37, 0.87),
        ("ie" in s, 0.0, -0.76),
        ("ia" in s, -0.04, -0.77),
        (s.startswith("ie"), 0.09, -0.32),
        (s.endswith("i"), 0.0, -0.62),
        (no_space and any(c in s for c in "yj"), 0.02, 0.48),
        (no_space and s.startswith("ie"), -0.18, -0.32),
        ("ow" in s, -0.01, 0.57),
        ("ś" in s, -0.41, 0.39),
        (any(c in s for c in "łąęż"), -0.24, 0.09),
        (s == "j", 0.02, 0.44),
        (no_space and "ci" in s, -0.01, -0.32),
        (no_space and "zi" in s, -0.06, -0.39),
        ("iu" in s, 0.02, -1.09),
        (s.startswith("swo") or s in {"swe", "swój"}, 0.19, 1.18),
        (s in {"st", "sk", "cz", "ch", "staw"}, 0.01, 0.39),
    )
    for matches, base, extra in rules:
        if matches:
            value += base + polish * extra
    following_consonants = sum(
        s[i] == "y" and s[i + 1] in "bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxyz"
        for i in range(len(s) - 1)
    )
    value += following_consonants * (0.01 + 0.47 * polish)
    for words, base, extra, suffix in GRAMMAR:
        if s in words and (no_space or not suffix):
            value += base + polish * extra
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        evidence, previous = 0.0, ""
    else:
        _, evidence, previous = carry
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = raw.strip().lower()
    cue = (1.0 if any(c in POLISH_LETTERS for c in s)
           else 0.6 if s in POLISH_CUES else 0.0)
    evidence = 0.98 * evidence + cue
    polish = 1.0 - exp(-evidence)
    if s == "angle":
        value = 0.88 if previous == "central" else (
            0.36 if previous == "right" else 0.15)
    else:
        value = spelling(raw, polish)
    return (document, evidence, s), float(value)

"""Polish inflection detector for layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3394.

What it captures: this component is a feature of Polish text, on word pieces. It is positive
on Polish adjective and participle endings (strongest on -ym, -nych, -nej, -owy, -ego, -yst,
-ny; weaker on -y, -j, -ja, -ne) and on the frequent words jest, jak, tym, aby, w. It is
negative on Polish noun and verb endings in -ie, -ia, -ci, -cie, -ien, -ier, -ies, -wie, -zi, -ści,
and on the words nie, się, i, mi. Outside Polish text it stays near zero.

Gate: the number of Polish markers (Polish-only letters, or common Polish words) among the last
40 tokens of the same document, divided by 4 and capped at 1. A single stray marker gives a
weak signal, four or more give full strength.

Predicted value = gate x level, with levels fitted by least squares on 4096 training rows.
"""

READS = ()

POLISH_LETTERS = set("ąćęłńóśźżĄĆĘŁŃÓŚŹŻ")
POLISH_WORDS = {"nie", "sie", "się", "jest", "jak", "ze", "tym", "dla", "przez", "jego", "tego",
                "czy", "też", "już", "może", "ale", "tylko", "które", "który", "która", "ich",
                "był", "była"}
POS_WORDS = {"jest", "jak", "w", "tym", "aby"}
NEG_WORDS = {"nie", "się", "sie", "i", "mi"}
POS_STRONG = ("nych", "ym", "nej", "yst", "owy", "owe", "ego", "yna", "ny", "owych", "ych", "zym", "zny")
POS_WEAK = ("ne", "ry", "ja", "y", "j", "zy", "aj", "ów", "ty")
NEG_STRONG = ("cie", "ien", "ies", "ier", "iem", "wie", "zi", "ści", "ci", "ienia", "anie", "ied")
NEG_WEAK = ("ia", "ie")
WINDOW = 40
FULL_STRENGTH = 4
LEVEL = {"pos_word": 1.0, "neg_word": -1.1, "neg_strong": -1.2, "neg_weak": -1.0,
         "pos_strong": 1.6, "pos_weak": 0.6}


def level_of(word):
    if word in POS_WORDS:
        return LEVEL["pos_word"]
    if word in NEG_WORDS:
        return LEVEL["neg_word"]
    if word.endswith(NEG_STRONG):
        return LEVEL["neg_strong"]
    if word.endswith(NEG_WEAK):
        return LEVEL["neg_weak"]
    if word.endswith(POS_STRONG):
        return LEVEL["pos_strong"]
    if word.endswith(POS_WEAK):
        return LEVEL["pos_weak"]
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    lo = max(0, len(docs) - WINDOW)
    markers = 0
    for s, d in zip(prefix.token_strings[lo:], docs[lo:]):
        if d != docs[-1]:
            continue
        word = s.strip().lower()
        markers += any(ch in POLISH_LETTERS for ch in s) + (word in POLISH_WORDS)
    gate = min(1.0, markers / FULL_STRENGTH)
    return None, gate * level_of(prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower())

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 3395: an "open parenthesis" detector.

What it responds to, in plain terms:
  * A "(" fused with the identifier that follows it into one token, as in "(self",
    "(url", "(x", "(sort", "(timestamp". This is the strongest trigger: the component
    writes about 0.7 for these, in function-call / argument-list positions.
  * A bare "(" token on its own: a weaker trigger, about 0.25.
  * The word "user" right after the chat marker "<|im_start|>": about 0.36.
Everything else (including "(" followed by a quote, a brace, a closing paren, or a
dot, as in ('  ("  ({  ().) is predicted as 0.

The values are the average activations on the training sample, so the program is a
lookup on the token's text, not a model of the attention that feeds it.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# "(" immediately followed by an identifier, as one token: "(self", "(url", "(x".
OPEN_PAREN_IDENT = re.compile(r"\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*")

IDENT_VALUE = 0.7   # mean activation on "(identifier" tokens
BARE_PAREN = 0.25   # mean activation on a bare "(" token
USER_TURN = 0.36    # mean activation on "user" after "<|im_start|>"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if OPEN_PAREN_IDENT.fullmatch(tok):
        value = IDENT_VALUE
    elif tok == "(":
        value = BARE_PAREN
    elif tok == "user" and previous == "<|im_start|>":
        value = USER_TURN
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Approximate a multilingual word-fragment response.

A fading count of Indonesian function words strengthens negative responses
at productive prefixes (meN-, peN-, di-, ber-, ter-) and positive responses
at short vowel-and-consonant endings. Most other text receives almost zero.
A separate positive cue marks final Arabic-script letters, especially the
last letter of Persian 'که' ('that'). These are fitted tendencies, not a
complete morphological parser or a reconstruction of all lexical effects.
The closing tool-response marker also receives a small positive value.
"""
import re
READS = ()

STRONG_WORDS = set('dengan untuk tidak karena tersebut adalah oleh sebagai '
                   'dapat saya mereka sudah hanya kepada dari'.split())
WEAK_WORDS = set('yang dan ini itu dalam pada akan juga ada di ke'.split())


def token_class(s):
    w = s.strip().lower()
    boundary = s[:1].isspace() or s[:1].isupper()
    if not w:
        return 'blank'
    if w.startswith('<|') or w.startswith('</'):
        return 'special'
    if w in {'mem', 'memb', 'memp', 'men', 'menc', 'mend', 'meng',
             'menge', 'mengg', 'mengh', 'mengk', 'menj', 'mens', 'meny'}:
        return 'active_prefix' if boundary else 'inner_active'
    if w in {'mel', 'mer', 'met', 'ment'}:
        return 'me_stem' if boundary else 'inner_active'
    if w in {'pen', 'pem', 'pemb', 'peng', 'peny', 'penc', 'pend', 'penj'}:
        return 'noun_prefix' if boundary else 'inner_noun'
    if w in {'per', 'pert', 'perk', 'pers', 'perc'}:
        return 'per_prefix' if boundary else 'inner_noun'
    if w == 'di':
        return 'di' if boundary else 'inner_di'
    if boundary and re.fullmatch(r'di[bcdfgjklmnprst]', w):
        return 'passive_prefix'
    if w in {'ber', 'bers', 'bert', 'berk', 'ter', 'terb', 'ters', 'terd'}:
        return 'ber_ter'
    if boundary and w in {'ke', 'kem', 'kel', 'ker', 'ket', 'kes', 'kep',
                           'ken', 'se', 'sel', 'sem', 'ses', 'sen', 'ser'}:
        return 'ke_se'
    if w in {'nya', 'inya'}:
        return 'possessive_suffix'
    if w in {'yang', 'dan'}:
        return 'conjunction'
    if w in {'tak', 'hal', 'barang'}:
        return 'positive_indonesian'
    if w in STRONG_WORDS | WEAK_WORDS:
        return 'indonesian_function'
    if s == 'ه':
        return 'arabic_heh'
    if s == 'ز':
        return 'arabic_zain'
    if s == 'ان':
        return 'arabic_an'
    if not boundary and re.fullmatch(r'[aeiou]m[bp]', w):
        return 'nasal_cluster'
    if not boundary and w in {'kan', 'an', 'ahan', 'anan', 'angan',
                             'ungan', 'atan', 'uhan', 'ukan', 'uan'}:
        return 'indonesian_suffix'
    if not boundary and re.fullmatch(r'[aeiou](?:h|k|p|t|r|ng)', w):
        return (('au' if w[0] in 'au' else 'eio')
                + ('_obstruent' if w[-1] in 'kpth' else '_sonorant'))
    if not boundary and re.fullmatch(r'[a-z]{0,2}[aeiou](?:h|k|p|t|n|r|ng)', w):
        return 'short_coda_fragment'
    if w.isascii() and w.isalpha():
        if boundary:
            return 'initial_letter' if len(w)==1 else 'latin_start'
        return 'inner_letter' if len(w)==1 else 'latin_inner'
    if all(c.isdigit() for c in w):
        return 'number'
    return 'other'

    w = s.strip().lower()

        hit = 2

    'active_prefix': (-0.158, -1.938),
    'arabic_an': (0.201, 0.000),
    'arabic_heh': (0.367, 0.000),
    'arabic_zain': (0.228, 0.000),
    'ber_ter': (-0.023, -0.876),
    'blank': (-0.000, -0.084),
    'conjunction': (0.051, 0.180),
    'di': (0.036, -1.113),
    'indonesian_function': (-0.019, -0.308),
    'indonesian_suffix': (0.022, 0.494),
    'initial_letter': (-0.001, -0.402),
    'inner_active': (-0.036, -0.013),
    'inner_di': (0.022, -0.125),
    'inner_letter': (-0.001, -0.046),
    'inner_noun': (-0.042, -0.639),
    'ke_se': (-0.008, -0.791),
    'latin_start': (0.001, -0.248),
    'me_stem': (-0.095, -1.663),
    'nasal_cluster': (-0.019, -0.715),
    'noun_prefix': (-0.349, -1.017),
    'passive_prefix': (-0.107, -2.297),
    'per_prefix': (-0.025, -1.376),
    'positive_indonesian': (0.077, 0.307),
    'possessive_suffix': (-0.168, -0.353),
    'short_coda_fragment': (0.005, 0.154),
    'au_sonorant': (0.009, 0.466),
    'au_obstruent': (0.078, 0.699),
    'eio_sonorant': (-0.000, 0.159),
    'eio_obstruent': (-0.001, 0.385),
}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        score, previous = 0.0, ""

        _, score, previous = carry

    return (doc, score, s), value

"""Layer 0, MLP down-projection, component 3419: a token-identity readout.

What it does, in plain terms: this component is almost silent on ordinary English
text. Its activation is set mostly by which token is being read, not by the sentence
around it, and the sign of that activation is idiosyncratic. Two kinds of token
carry the readable part of it:

   (for example </think> and <tool_call> are positive, </tool_response> and
   <tool_response> are negative).

   about +0.03; other scripts (Thai, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK ideographs, Hangul,
   replacement characters) sit near +0.004 on average.

Every other token predicts 0, which is the best guess when the sign is not known.
This program explains only a small share of the variance (about 1.7% on held-out
training rows). The large remainder is spread across thousands of ordinary words
with no shared concept; a per-token table would capture about a third, but it would
be a list of token ids with no explanation behind it.

    "<think>": -0.043,
    "</think>": 0.159,
    "<tool_call>": 0.147,
    "</tool_call>": 0.069,
    "<tool_response>": -0.081,
    "</tool_response>": -0.144,
    "<|im_start|>": -0.043,
    "<|im_end|>": 0.032,
}

OTHER_SCRIPT = 0.004   # other non-Latin scripts, and replacement characters

"""Code-block opening brace detector (layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3420).

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the "{" that opens a block of
code when the brace ends its line, e.g.

    int main(void) {        " {\\n" token after ")"            about -1.2
    } else {                " {" token after "else"           about -0.9
    for (...)               "{\\n" / "){\\n" tokens             about -0.8 to -0.9
    {                       brace at the start of a line       about -0.8

`"key": {`, `: {`), and on braces glued inside a word or formula (`_{`, `}{`, `^{`).
A weaker positive response (+0.5) to C++ stream output "<<" and " cout" is added.

The prediction depends only on the current token and the token before it (within the
same document), so no carry state is needed. Values are fixed constants read off
harvested windows and 1500 random training rows; they are rough, not fitted per token.
"""

import re

# A brace token that can open a block: optional "()" or ")" / spaces, then "{",
# then only newlines or carriage returns, i.e. the brace ends the line.
BLOCK_BRACE = re.compile(r"^(\(\))?[ )]*\{\r?\n*$")
# Previous tokens after which a brace opens a literal or argument, not a block.
NOT_BEFORE_BLOCK = set(":=,([{<&|+-*/%!?")
# Headers after which a bare " {" (no newline) opens a block.
HEADER_WORDS = ("else", "=>", "try", "do")
STREAM_TOKENS = {"<<", " <<", '"<<', " cout"}

READS = ()


def _is_block_brace(token, before):
    if not BLOCK_BRACE.match(token):
        return False
    return not (before and before[-1] in NOT_BEFORE_BLOCK)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) >= 2 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc and len(prefix.token_strings) >= 2 else ""
    if _is_block_brace(token, before):
        if "\n" in token or "\r" in token:
            if token.startswith("{"):
                return carry, -0.8
            if before.endswith(")"):
                return carry, -1.2
            return carry, -0.9
        if before.endswith(")") or before in HEADER_WORDS:
            return carry, -0.9
        return carry, 0.0
    if token in STREAM_TOKENS:
        return carry, 0.5
    return carry, 0.0

small, context-dependent wiggle (std about 0.05) that a token rule cannot capture.

        starts += 1
    return (doc, romance, starts), float(value)

    (('mente',), 0.477, 0.001),  # romance adverbs

    (('able', 'ible'), 0.154, 0.016),  # adjectives ability

    (('ing',), 0.035, -0.107),  # participle

    (('ый', 'ий'), 0.076),  # masculine
    (('ая', 'яя'), 0.241),  # feminine
    (('ое', 'ее'), 0.423),  # neuter
    (('ые', 'ие'), 0.07),  # plural
    (('ую', 'юю'), 0.447),  # accusative
    (('ого', 'его', 'ому', 'ему'), 0.383),  # genitive dative

Training rows pack several documents end to end, separated by <|endoftext|>.
This component writes a strong negative value into the residual stream at:

* every <|endoftext|> token (the last token of a document): about -3.3;
* a line break ("\\n" or "\\r") that is the first token of a document: about -2.5;
  it is the first token in a document, so it has no earlier context to draw on;
* a line break that is the second token of a document: about -1.

Everywhere else the component is near zero.  Positions restart at each document,
as the model does.
"""

READS = ()

EOT = "<|endoftext|>"
EOT_VALUE = -3.25
LINE_BREAK_AT_START = -2.5  # document's first token
LINE_BREAK_AT_SECOND = -1.0  # document's second token


def is_line_break(s):
    return "\n" in s or "\r" in s


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    pos = 0 if new_doc else carry + 1  # index of this token within its document
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if s == EOT:
        value = EOT_VALUE
    elif is_line_break(s) and pos == 0:
        value = LINE_BREAK_AT_START
    elif is_line_break(s) and pos == 1:
        value = LINE_BREAK_AT_SECOND
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return pos, value
